domain_assessment.role: SIGINT desk analyst in a regional fusion cell
domain_assessment.objective: Produce a confidence-graded assessment of whether anomalous encrypted traffic near the Sector 7 logistics hub indicated an operational logistics buildup or routine activity.
domain_assessment.incident_type: Time-constrained assessment of anomalous communications using incomplete translation, historical baselines, open-source reporting, and IMINT corroboration.

decision_points.summary: Allocate scarce linguist time between the strategically important Sector 7 spike and the statistically more unusual Sector 4 anomaly.
evidence_before: Sector 7 had encrypted burst traffic well above baseline near a known logistics node.
Sector 4 had a smaller but less typical statistical pattern.
No message content was yet available.
Only three linguist-hours were available before a six-hour briefing deadline.
evidence_after: Partial Sector 7 translations contained convoy language, resupply terms, unexplained coded phrases, and routine rotation talk.
goals_constraints: Brief the fusion-cell lead within six hours.
alternatives: Prioritize Sector 4 because its signal pattern was more unusual.
Prioritize Sector 7 because of its strategic consequence.
decision_points.decision_basis: Sector 7 was prioritized because a possible development at a strategically significant logistics hub had greater operational consequence under the deadline.
decision_points.time_pressure: High: six-hour briefing deadline and an existing translation backlog.
decision_points.uncertainty: High: the initial decision relied on signal signatures and historical baselines rather than message content.

decision_points.summary: Construct and provisionally privilege an emerging-logistics-buildup explanation from mixed, partial translations and the signal pattern.
evidence_before: Sector 7 burst-traffic surge.
Partial convoy and resupply terminology.
Two unresolved coded phrases.
Routine rotation talk.
An exercise-calendar rotation window.
No imagery corroboration.
evidence_after: A later intercept contained maintenance-cycle terminology.
One coded phrase was later identified in a maintenance-schedule glossary.
goals_constraints: Form a usable working hypothesis from incomplete evidence.
Draft an intelligible assessment under time pressure.
Distinguish possible buildup from rotation or maintenance activity.
alternatives: Lead with an emerging logistics-buildup account.
Lead with a rotation or maintenance account.
decision_points.decision_basis: The analyst judged the buildup account to explain more observed details and became more confident after organizing those details into a coherent written sequence.
decision_points.time_pressure: Moderate to high: the analyst was drafting toward the fixed briefing deadline.
decision_points.uncertainty: High: translations were partial, code terms were unresolved, and a plausible rotation explanation remained available.

decision_points.summary: Select and weight an easily processed open-source digest over a denser but more location-specific IMINT report.
evidence_before: The digest was well-written, clearly formatted, and forecast regional tension consistent with the draft.
The IMINT report addressed vehicle dispersal at the Sector 7 hub.
The IMINT report was dense and heavy with sensor terminology.
The IMINT analyst was unavailable for a walk-through.
The analyst believed there was time to fully absorb only one source.
evidence_after: The IMINT dispersal pattern was later found to be consistent with both maintenance stand-down and buildup.
The digest was based on general regional reporting rather than Sector 7-specific reporting.
goals_constraints: Obtain usable corroboration before the briefing.
alternatives: Use the digest as primary corroboration.
Prioritize the more directly relevant IMINT report.
Weight both sources cautiously and limit the corroboration claim.
Use neither as meaningful corroboration pending fuller assessment.
decision_points.decision_basis: The analyst chose the digest because it was easy to process and integrate into the draft; its fluent presentation made general regional reporting feel more directly applicable to Sector 7 than the content could support.
decision_points.time_pressure: High: the analyst could fully process only one source before the deadline.
decision_points.uncertainty: Moderate to high: IMINT interpretation competence was limited, and the digest's Sector 7 relevance was not established.

decision_points.summary: Set final confidence at moderate, lead with a buildup assessment, disclose the maintenance contradiction, and request follow-up collection.
evidence_before: A coherent buildup narrative.
Partial open-source support.
Maintenance terminology inconsistent with the buildup account.
No definitive imagery assessment.
Twenty minutes before the briefing.
evidence_after: The lead accepted the moderate assessment and tasked follow-up collection.
Follow-up traffic remained mixed after two days.
goals_constraints: Provide an actionable assessment without overstating certainty.
Recommend collection capable of reducing uncertainty.
alternatives: Moderate-confidence buildup assessment with an explicit contradiction and follow-up tasking.
decision_points.decision_basis: The analyst selected moderate confidence because the observed pattern appeared operationally meaningful but the maintenance contradiction precluded high confidence.
decision_points.time_pressure: Very high: twenty minutes remained before the briefing.
decision_points.uncertainty: High: evidence continued to support multiple plausible explanations.

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “Writing it out that way, it held together. It read like a coherent sequence, and honestly, once I had it typed up in that form, I felt more confident it was the right read than when I'd started.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Decision point 2; response following the description of the first partial translation batch.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The participant explicitly reports increased confidence after constructing a coherent causal account from evidence already available. The confidence increase is attributed to writing and organizing the narrative, not to the arrival of new corroborating evidence.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: Writing can legitimately improve evidence organization. Here, however, the participant specifically links greater confidence to narrative coherence despite unresolved coded phrases, rotation evidence, and the absence of imagery corroboration.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: None. The interview identifies the reasoning operation, unchanged evidence base, confidence change, and relevant competing explanation.

revision.current_defect: None material. The occurrence is independently identifiable and distinct from the source-selection episode.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: Retain the existing temporal and causal sequence: partial evidence, written narrative construction, then increased confidence without new supporting evidence.
avoid_creating: A second explanation-bias occurrence at final confidence calibration
Explicit naming of the bias in participant language
Language treating narrative coherence as objective proof

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “It read so cleanly and confidently that its regional forecast felt like it applied straight to Sector 7, more than I could really back up just from what was on the page.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Decision point 3; participant explanation immediately after describing the digest as quick to read and easy to integrate into the write-up.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The analyst describes a source-selection and evidentiary-weighting error in which polished, easily processed presentation increased the apparent applicability of broad regional reporting to Sector 7. The participant acknowledges that this felt relevance exceeded what the digest's content could substantiate, while also recognizing that IMINT was more specific to the hub.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: Time pressure and limited ability to interpret IMINT are legitimate constraints, but they do not explain the separate stated inference that the digest's clear and confident presentation made its regional forecast seem more Sector 7-specific than the underlying evidence warranted.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: None. The interview now directly identifies ease and presentation fluency as causing inflated perceived relevance, rather than merely establishing a rational preference for a usable source.

revision.current_defect: None material. The added self-report distinguishes presentation-driven perceived applicability from valid source relevance.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: Retain the admission that the digest seemed to apply directly to Sector 7 because it read clearly and confidently, despite insufficient Sector 7-specific support.
preserve: The IMINT report's greater location specificity
The time constraint and lack of IMINT analyst support
The later finding that IMINT remained substantively ambiguous
avoid_creating: A second fluency-effects episode elsewhere in the interview
An overt textbook explanation of source fluency
A claim that the IMINT report definitively disproved buildup
Making agreement with the buildup draft the sole or clearly dominant reason for selection

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “The digest was quick to read and slotted right into the write-up I already had going—it reinforced the framing.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: The selected digest aligned with the already drafted buildup account and was easier to integrate than the more difficult IMINT report.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The account establishes that processing fluency and time pressure were material drivers. It does not establish that agreement with the buildup hypothesis was independently decisive, nor that contradictory material was deliberately avoided.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “Once it was written that clearly, it was hard to hold as loosely as I probably should have.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: The initial buildup framing may have made later contradictory maintenance information psychologically harder to treat as equally diagnostic.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: This is best treated as retrospective elaboration of the supported explanation-bias episode, not a separate occurrence. The analyst did incorporate the contradictory evidence, reduce final confidence, and request discriminating collection.

nonbias_cues.cue: Prioritizing Sector 7 rather than Sector 4 for limited translation.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: The decision is grounded in stated operational consequence, strategic relevance, limited linguist capacity, and a deadline. Sector 4's greater statistical unusualness does not make it necessarily more important to investigate first.

nonbias_cues.cue: Considering convoy and resupply language compatible with a logistics buildup.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: This is a plausible hypothesis-generation step based on partial evidence. It is not biased merely because another explanation later remains viable.

nonbias_cues.cue: Concern that a dense IMINT report could be misread without technical support.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Recognizing one's limits in interpreting unfamiliar sensor terminology can be sound epistemic risk management. The fluency occurrence rests instead on inflated perceived relevance of the digest due to its presentation.

nonbias_cues.cue: Moderate confidence, explicit acknowledgment of maintenance terminology, and a recommendation for follow-up collection.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: This represents appropriate calibration and uncertainty management. The later unresolved follow-up traffic does not retroactively establish a cognitive bias.

nonbias_cues.cue: The lead accepting the assessment and ordering follow-up collection.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: A supervisor's response and a procedurally appropriate collection task do not independently validate or invalidate the analyst's reasoning process.

causal_claims.claim: Convoy references, burst traffic, and unexplained coded phrases support an emerging logistics-buildup account.
causal_claims.assessment: A plausible analytic hypothesis, but not a demonstrated causal conclusion. The evidence may also arise from rotation or maintenance activity.

causal_claims.claim: Unexplained coded phrases likely represented concealment of non-plain-language operational activity.
causal_claims.assessment: Initially weak. The later identification of one phrase as maintenance-related shows that unexplained terminology should not itself be treated as evidence of concealment.

causal_claims.claim: Narrative construction increased confidence in the buildup account.
causal_claims.assessment: Strongly supported as a self-reported cognitive-process claim, and it is the relevant explanation-bias mechanism.

causal_claims.claim: The digest's fluent presentation made its regional forecast feel directly applicable to Sector 7.
causal_claims.assessment: Strongly supported as a self-reported cognitive-process claim. The participant explicitly acknowledges that this perceived applicability exceeded what the source content could justify.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: The buildup account groups co-occurring traffic volume, convoy language, resupply terms, and coded phrases into one causal interpretation without establishing that the indicators arose from a common operation.
correlation_causation_risks.mitigation_present: The interview preserves competing rotation and maintenance explanations, notes absent imagery corroboration, and reports a moderate rather than high-confidence final assessment.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: General regional-tension reporting is treated as partial corroboration for a Sector 7-specific claim.
correlation_causation_risks.mitigation_present: The participant later learns that the digest did not specifically tie its reporting to Sector 7 and retrospectively recognizes overextension of its applicability.

causal_audit.changed_variable: Availability of corroborating sources: the counterfactual removes the open-source digest, leaving the IMINT report as the only corroborating option.
held_constant: The underlying traffic spike and translated-intercept evidence
The lack of a quick IMINT analyst walk-through
causal_audit.explanation: The counterfactual changes one identifiable variable and elicits a coherent predicted pathway: without the fluent digest, the analyst would spend more effort on IMINT, recognize ambiguity sooner, and hedge more. It is a retrospective self-report rather than independent causal proof, but it is internally consistent and does not introduce a second material causal change.

global_revision_constraints: Keep explanation bias at the working-note construction episode in decision point 2.
Keep fluency effects at source selection and evidentiary weighting in decision point 3.
Do not treat the unresolved operational outcome as proof of either bias.
Preserve the analyst's appropriate final acknowledgment of contradictory evidence and follow-up collection recommendation.
Avoid amplifying the weak confirmation-bias cue into a distinct unintended occurrence.
